title: Jordan Stolz ends Milan Olympics with 3 medals after 4th-place showing in mass start
content:
MILAN — In a bid for his fourth Olympic medal, speedskater Jordan Stolz came up short.

Stolz, who already secured stardom as the most decorated individual American athlete at the Milan Cortina Olympics, finished fourth in the mass start event Saturday.

“I would say it’s pretty successful,” Stolz said of his second Winter Games, which included Olympic records in the 1,000-meter and 500-meter races. “There’s things that could have gone better, but two golds and a silver, I’m pretty happy with that.”

Jorrit Bergsma, a 40-year-old Dutch skater who was this season’s World Cup champion in the mass start, set a blistering pace early and crushed the competition. He is the oldest long-track speedskater to win gold in any event.

Bergsma moved away from the pack just a few laps into the 16-lap race, creating an early gulf and a quandary for Stolz: push the pace and end up with dead legs at the end, or hang back and not allow the rest of the group to draft off him?

Stolz said repeatedly that if he had pushed the early pace and tried to catch Bergsma, he would have faded and ended up off the podium as well.

“If I would have known that they would have been reluctant to chase, even when none of the guys (hanging back) have a medal, I probably would have attacked a little bit more,” Stolz said, “but if I would have done that, they still would have just followed me and (it) would’ve just canceled out.”

Bergsma finished with a time of 7 minutes, 55.50 seconds, with Denmark’s Viktor Hald Thorup winning silver more than five seconds behind him at 8:00.52. Italy’s Andrea Giovannini took the bronze, finishing nine hundredths of a second ahead of Stolz, who crossed the finish line at 8:04.51.

Stolz said with about five laps to go, as Hald had also pulled away, he realized the rest of the group was fighting for third.

“I actually didn’t expect this to happen,” Stolz said. “Just because I felt like the gold medal favorites from mass start were going to be more hungry to try and get a medal, but they all were just kind of expecting me to go for it, and, yeah, it didn’t really work.”

Despite coming up empty-handed in the mass start, Stolz will leave Milan as the most decorated U.S. Winter Olympian since fellow speed skater Eric Heiden won five golds in 1980. Stolz had a terrific showing in Milan, starting with a gold in the 1,000m and then 500m. He won the silver in the 1,500 meters on Thursday as China’s Ning Zhongyan had the best skate of his career.

Still, Stolz will go back to Wisconsin as one of the American faces of the Milan Games.

“I’ve had some great races here,” said Stolz, who is still just 21 years old. “Some could have been better, but I think it’s actually a good result, I’ll continue to improve and, two golds and a silver, that’s pretty good.”

Asked if his life had changed much since he got to Milan, Stolz said he’s been pretty focused.

He skipped the opening ceremony to stay off his feet and has been diligent about his schedule and nutrition. Even now, with three medals and all four events behind him, Stolz is already looking forward to his next race, the World Cup, and continuing to push his limit.

“I will try and attempt the sprints and the all-around, which is four days,” he said. “I don’t know if anyone’s ever done that before. We’ll see if I can pull that off.”
